  • Method Details

    • getPhone

      @RequestMapping(method=GET, value="/api/account/phone", produces={"application/json","application/problem+json"}) org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<PhoneResponse> getPhone()
      GET /api/account/phone : Gets the verified phone number Answers the verified phone number of the authenticated account, masked so that only its last digits are shown. A number whose verification is still pending is not reported, and neither is any number of another account.
      Returns:
      The verified phone number (status code 200) or Missing or invalid bearer token (status code 401) or The account has no verified phone number (problem type urn:problem:phone:phone-not-found) (status code 404)

    • removePhone

      @RequestMapping(method=DELETE, value="/api/account/phone", produces="application/problem+json") org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<Void> removePhone()
      DELETE /api/account/phone : Removes the phone number Removes the verified phone number and any pending verification of the authenticated account, so SMS codes can no longer be used, and audits the removal; when the account is then left without any confirmed second factor, every trusted device of the account is revoked. Removing a phone that is not set succeeds as well. While the account has a confirmed second factor, the bearer token must show a recent multi-factor sign-in (step-up, RFC 9470).
      Returns:
      The phone number is removed (status code 204) or Missing or invalid bearer token (an RFC 6750 challenge and no body), or the account has a confirmed second factor and the token does not show a multi-factor sign-in (acr urn:irurueta:acr:mfa) whose auth_time is within authserver.mfa.step-up-max-age (default 5 minutes). The latter is answered as RFC 9470 describes, with WWW-Authenticate Bearer error=\"insufficient_user_authentication\", acr_values=\"urn:irurueta:acr:mfa\", max_age=\"300\" (the configured age in seconds) and a problem body; the client signs the user in again with those acr_values and max_age and retries with the new token. (status code 401)

    • startPhoneEnrolment

      @RequestMapping(method=PUT, value="/api/account/phone", produces={"application/json","application/problem+json"}, consumes="application/json") org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<PhoneEnrolmentResponse> startPhoneEnrolment(@Valid @RequestBody @Valid StartPhoneEnrolmentRequest startPhoneEnrolmentRequest)
      PUT /api/account/phone : Starts the enrolment of a phone number Normalises the number to E.164 (a number without a country prefix is read in the default region of the server), checks that SMS messages may be sent to its country and sends a verification code by SMS. The enrolment is pending until it is confirmed with the code on POST /api/account/phone/verify; starting it again replaces the pending one. The answer is the same whether or not the number already belongs to another account, and in that case no message is sent, so the endpoint never reveals which numbers are registered. The message is sent after the answer, so a slow or failing SMS gateway never shows in it. Limited per client address and per account. While the account has a confirmed second factor (the new number would replace the verified one), the bearer token must show a recent multi-factor sign-in (step-up, RFC 9470).
      Parameters:
      startPhoneEnrolmentRequest - (required)
      Returns:
      The verification code was requested (status code 202) or The request is invalid, the number is not a valid phone number (problem type urn:problem:phone:invalid-phone) or SMS messages are not sent to its country (problem type urn:problem:phone:country-not-allowed) (status code 400) or Missing or invalid bearer token (an RFC 6750 challenge and no body), or the account has a confirmed second factor and the token does not show a multi-factor sign-in (acr urn:irurueta:acr:mfa) whose auth_time is within authserver.mfa.step-up-max-age (default 5 minutes). The latter is answered as RFC 9470 describes, with WWW-Authenticate Bearer error=\"insufficient_user_authentication\", acr_values=\"urn:irurueta:acr:mfa\", max_age=\"300\" (the configured age in seconds) and a problem body; the client signs the user in again with those acr_values and max_age and retries with the new token. (status code 401) or Too many requests from this client or for this address (status code 429)

    • verifyPhone

      @RequestMapping(method=POST, value="/api/account/phone/verify", produces={"application/json","application/problem+json"}, consumes="application/json") org.springframework.http.ResponseEntity<PhoneResponse> verifyPhone(@Valid @RequestBody @Valid VerifyPhoneRequest verifyPhoneRequest)
      POST /api/account/phone/verify : Confirms the phone number with the code sent by SMS Checks the code against the pending verification of the authenticated account. A correct code makes the number the verified phone of the account; a wrong one counts as an attempt, and the verification is discarded after too many. A number that replaces another verified one is audited as the removal of a second factor and revokes every trusted device of the account. Limited per client address and per account.
      Parameters:
      verifyPhoneRequest - (required)
      Returns:
      The phone number is verified (status code 200) or The request is invalid, or the code is wrong, expired or there is no verification in progress (problem type urn:problem:phone:invalid-code) (status code 400) or Missing or invalid bearer token (status code 401) or Too many requests from this client or for this address (status code 429)
